extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (number theorists, computational algebraists, and developers using the PARI/GP algebra libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions operating on central simple algebras and table algebras: each entry states the function purpose, inputs, return values, examples, and any warnings or special behavior. Intended to guide correct use and interpretation of results when manipulating algebras, lattices, Hasse invariants, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: algcharpoly(al, b, {v = -1}, {abs})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and an element b (or a square matrix with coefficients in al), returns the characteristic polynomial of b. When abs = 1, returns the characteristic polynomial of the element seen over the prime subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage with al produced by alginit and nfinit; accepts square matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algcharpoly(GEN al, GEN b, long v = -1, long abs).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdegree(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns the degree of al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: algdegree(A) returns 2 for a quaternion algebra. Library syntax: long algdegree(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdim(al, {abs = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: If al is a table algebra output by algtableinit or if abs = 1, returns the dimension of al over its prime subfield (Q or Fp). If al is a central simple algebra output by alginit and abs = 0, returns the dimension of al over its center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate algdim(A) and algdim(A,1). Library syntax: long algdim(GEN al, long abs).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdisc(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, computes the discriminant of the order O0 stored in al, i.e. the determinant of the trace form Tr: O0 × O0 → Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing ancillary quantities and confirms algdisc(A) equals expected integer. Library syntax: GEN algdisc(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdivl(al, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two elements x and y in al, computes their left quotient x\y in the algebra al: an element z such that x*z = y (not unique when x is a zero divisor). Assumes y is left divisible by x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is invertible, this equals x^{-1}y. Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algdivl(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdivr(al, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two elements x and y in al, returns x*y^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algdivr(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: alggroup(gal, {p = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes the group algebra K[G] over K = Q (p omitted) or Fp where G is the underlying group of a galoisinit structure gal; gal may also be a t_VEC of permutations closed under product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows constructing al from galoisinit(K) and testing semisimplicity. Library syntax: GEN alggroup(GEN gal, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alggroupcenter(gal, {p = 0}, {&cc})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes the center Z(K[G]) of the group algebra K[G] over K = Q (p = 0 or omitted) or Fp where G is from galoisinit or a closed t_VEC of permutations. Sets cc to [elts, conjclass, rep, flag] describing elements, conjugacy classes, representatives and transitivity flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis of Z(K[G]) returned consists of indicator functions of conjugacy classes ordered by cc. Examples and cc component semantics provided. Library syntax: GEN alggroupcenter(GEN gal, GEN p = NULL, GEN *cc = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alghasse(al, pl)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al and a prime ideal or an integer between 1 and r1+r2, returns the local Hasse invariant of al at the specified place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show alghasse(A,1) or alghasse(A,idealprimedec(nf,2)[1]) returning rationals like 1/2 or 0. Library syntax: GEN alghasse(GEN al, GEN pl).

rubrics_metrics.name: alghassef(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns a t_VEC [PR, hf] describing the local Hasse invariants at the finite places of the center: PR is a t_VEC of primes and hf is a t_VECSMALL of integers modulo the degree d of al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hasse invariant outside PR is 0; PR may include primes with invariant 0. Example demonstrates returned PR and hf. Library syntax: GEN alghassef(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: alghassei(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns a t_VECSMALL hi of r1 integers modulo the degree d of al, the local Hasse invariants at the infinite (real) places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: alghassei(A) returns Vecsmall([1,0]). Library syntax: GEN alghassei(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algindex(al, {pl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the index of the central simple algebra A over K (the degree e of the unique central division algebra D with A ≅ M_k(D)). If pl specified (prime ideal or integer between 1 and r1+r2), returns the local index at that place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show local and global algindex outputs. Library syntax: long algindex(GEN al, GEN pl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alginit(B, C, {v}, {maxord = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes the central simple algebra defined by data B, C and variable v. Multiple construction modes: multiplication table over K; cyclic algebra from rnf structure; quaternion algebra special case; algebra defined by local Hasse invariants; matrix algebra (Md(K)). Computes a maximal order by default unless maxord=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive examples for each construction mode provided: (multiplication table), (cyclic algebra with [sigma,b]), (quaternion with [a,b]), (Hasse invariants triple [d,[PR,hf],hi]), (matrix algebra). The function stores splitting field, Hasse invariants, bases, multiplication tables, characteristic, absolute traces, and possible cyclic algebra data. Warning: computing maximal order may be time-consuming. Library syntax: GEN alginit(GEN B, GEN C, long v = -1, long maxord).

rubrics_metrics.name: alginv(al, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its inverse x^{-1} in the algebra al. Assumes x is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example and library syntax: GEN alginv(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: alginvbasis(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns a Z-basis of the natural order in al with respect to the order O0 stored in al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows 4×4 basis output. Library syntax: GEN alginvbasis(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algisassociative(mt, p = 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if the multiplication table mt is suitable for algtableinit(mt,p), 0 otherwise; checks e1 = 1 and associativity ei(ej*ek) = (ei*ej)ek for all i,j,k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used to check an algebra a posteriori; mt may be as output of algtableinit (p ignored). Example demonstrates usage. Library syntax: GEN algisassociative(GEN mt, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: algiscommutative(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether the algebra al (table algebra from algtableinit or central simple algebra from alginit) is commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show both commutative and non-commutative cases. Library syntax: GEN algiscommutative(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algisdivision(al, {pl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, tests whether al is a division algebra. If pl provided (prime ideal or integer between 1 and r1+r2), tests whether al is locally a division algebra at place pl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show local/global checks returning 0/1. Library syntax: GEN algisdivision(GEN al, GEN pl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algisdivl(al, x, y, {&z})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given x and y in al, tests whether y is left divisible by x (exists z with x*z = y); if &z provided, sets z when it exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example shows return 0 or 1 and setting z. Library syntax: GEN algisdivl(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y, GEN *z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algisinv(al, x, {&ix})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, tests whether x is invertible; if &ix present, sets ix to inverse of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example demonstrates ix being set when invertible. Library syntax: GEN algisinv(GEN al, GEN x, GEN *ix = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algisramified(al, {pl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, tests whether al is ramified (i.e. not isomorphic to a matrix algebra over its center). If pl set, tests whether al is locally ramified at the place pl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show algisramified(A,1) etc. Library syntax: GEN algisramified(GEN al, GEN pl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algissemisimple(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: al being a table algebra output by algtableinit or a central simple algebra output by alginit, tests whether the algebra al is semisimple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show semisimple and non-semisimple outputs. Library syntax: GEN algissemisimple(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algissimple(al, {ss = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether the algebra al is simple. If ss = 1, assumes al is semisimple without testing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate difference between testing and assuming ss=1. Library syntax: GEN algissimple(GEN al, long ss).

rubrics_metrics.name: algissplit(al, {pl})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, tests whether al is split (isomorphic to a matrix algebra over its center). If pl set, tests whether al is locally split at pl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show local and global split tests. Library syntax: GEN algissplit(GEN al, GEN pl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatadd(al, lat1, lat2, {&ptinter})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and two lattices lat1 and lat2 in al, computes the sum lat1 + lat2. If ptinter provided, sets it to the intersection lat1 ∩ lat2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes latsum and latinter determinants. Library syntax: GEN alglatadd(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2, GEN *ptinter = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatcontains(al, lat, x, {&ptc})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al, a lattice lat and x in al, tests whether x ∈ lat. If ptc present, sets it to coordinates of x in basis of lat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates setting coordinate vector c. Library syntax: GEN alglatcontains(GEN al, GEN lat, GEN x, GEN *ptc = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatelement(al, lat, c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al, a lattice lat and a t_COL c, returns the element of al whose coordinates on the Z-basis of lat are given by c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows alglatelement and verifying coordinates via alglatcontains. Library syntax: GEN alglatelement(GEN al, GEN lat, GEN c).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglathnf(al, m, {d = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and a matrix m with columns representing elements of al, returns the lattice L generated by the columns of m. If provided, d must be a rational such that L contains d times the natural basis of al. m may be t_VEC of t_MAT or a t_COL (interpreted as left multiplication table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs mt = algtomatrix(al,a,1) then lat = alglathnf(al,mt). Library syntax: GEN alglathnf(GEN al, GEN m, GEN d).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatindex(al, lat1, lat2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and two lattices lat1 and lat2, computes the generalized index of lat1 relative to lat2: |lat2/(lat1 ∩ lat2)| / |lat1/(lat1 ∩ lat2)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses alglathnf to create lattices and alglatindex(al,lat1,lat2). Library syntax: GEN alglatindex(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatinter(al, lat1, lat2, {&ptsum})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and two lattices lat1 and lat2, computes the intersection lat1 ∩ lat2. If ptsum present, sets it to the sum lat1 + lat2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes latinter and latsum and their determinants. Library syntax: GEN alglatinter(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2, GEN *ptsum = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatlefttransporter(al, lat1, lat2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and lattices lat1 and lat2, computes the left transporter: set of x ∈ al such that x · lat1 ⊂ lat2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs tr and verifies alglatsubset(al,alglatmul(al,a,lat1),lat2). Library syntax: GEN alglatlefttransporter(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatmul(al, lat1, lat2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and two lattices lat1 and lat2, computes the lattice generated by products of elements of lat1 and lat2. One of lat1 or lat2 may be an element of al (then product of element and lattice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage and comparisons. Library syntax: GEN alglatmul(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatrighttransporter(al, lat1, lat2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and lattices lat1 and lat2, computes the right transporter: set of x ∈ al such that lat1 · x ⊂ lat2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs tr and verifies containment. Library syntax: GEN alglatrighttransporter(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2).

rubrics_metrics.name: alglatsubset(al, lat1, lat2, {&ptindex})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and two lattices lat1 and lat2, tests whether lat1 ⊂ lat2. If ptindex present and true, sets it to the index of lat1 in lat2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show alglatsubset returning 0/1 and setting index when applicable. Library syntax: GEN alglatsubset(GEN al, GEN lat1, GEN lat2, GEN *ptindex = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algmakeintegral(mt, {maps = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: mt being a multiplication table over Q, computes an integral multiplication table for an isomorphic algebra. When maps = 1, returns [mt2, S, T] with maps S and T between algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows converting mt with denominators failing algtableinit then using algmakeintegral(mt) to obtain integral table and succeed. Library syntax: GEN algmakeintegral(GEN mt, long maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: algmul(al, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two elements x and y in al, computes their product x*y in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example and library syntax: GEN algmul(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: algmultable(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a multiplication table of al over its prime subfield (Q or Fp) as a t_VEC of t_MAT: the left multiplication tables of basis elements. If al from algtableinit, returns the original multiplication table; if from alginit, returns multiplication table of order O0 in al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example inspects M = algmultable(A) and shows M[1] is identity. Library syntax: GEN algmultable(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algneg(al, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its opposite -x in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algneg(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: algnorm(al, x, {abs = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its norm. If al is a table algebra or abs = 1, returns absolute norm in Fp or Q; if al is central simple algebra and abs = 0 (default), returns the reduced norm in the center of al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate both absolute and reduced norms and relations with nfeltnorm. Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algnorm(GEN al, GEN x, long abs).

rubrics_metrics.name: algpoleval(al, T, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element b in al and a polynomial T in K[X], computes T(b) in al. Also accepts [b,mb] where mb is left multiplication table of b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses algcharpoly and verifies algpoleval(al,pol,b) == 0. Library syntax: GEN algpoleval(GEN al, GEN T, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: algpow(al, x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al and integer n, computes x^n in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts square matrices with coefficients in al. Example: algpow(A,[1,1,0,0],7). Library syntax: GEN algpow(GEN al, GEN x, GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: algprimesubalg(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: al being output of algtableinit representing a semisimple algebra of positive characteristic, returns a basis of the prime subalgebra of al (subalgebra fixed by Frobenius of center), abstractly a product of copies of Fp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates output matrix. Library syntax: GEN algprimesubalg(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algquotient(al, I, {maps = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: al being a table algebra and I a basis matrix of a two-sided ideal, returns the quotient algebra al/I. When maps = 1 returns [al/I, proj, lift] with projection and section maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs AQ = algquotient(A,[0;1;0]) and verifies algdim(AQ). Library syntax: GEN alg_quotient(GEN al, GEN I, long maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: algradical(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: al being a table algebra output by algtableinit, returns a basis of the Jacobson radical of the algebra al over its prime field (Q or Fp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Q[x]/(x^2) and 2×2 upper triangular matrices, showing returned radical basis. Library syntax: GEN algradical(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algramifiedplaces(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns a t_VEC listing the places of the center that are ramified in al (each place as integer between 1 and r1 or as a prime ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example returns [1, [2, ...]] for a given algebra. Library syntax: GEN algramifiedplaces(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algrandom(al, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al and integer b, returns a random element in al with coefficients in [-b, b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN algrandom(GEN al, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: algrelmultable(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit defined by a multiplication table over its center (a number field), returns that relative multiplication table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples compare returned matrices to original m_i, m_j, m_k. Library syntax: GEN algrelmultable(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsimpledec(al, {maps = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: al being output of algtableinit, returns [J, [al1, al2, ..., aln]] where J is basis of Jacobson radical and al/J is isomorphic to direct product of simple algebras al_i. When maps=1, each al_i replaced by [al_i, proj_i, lift_i] with projection/section maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors are sorted by increasing dimension then center dimension. Note sorting determinism over finite fields may not hold over Q. Library syntax: GEN algsimpledec(GEN al, long maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplit(al, {v = 'x'})
rubrics_metrics.description: If al is a table algebra over Fp and represents a simple algebra, computes an isomorphism between al and a matrix algebra M_d(F_{p^n}) and returns [map, mapi], where map gives images of basis elements and mapi gives inverse image representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: map is t_VEC of N matrices representing image of basis; mapi is N×N integer matrix mapping basis of Md(Fp[α]) back. Warning: if al is not simple, algsplit(al) can error or loop indefinitely. Example shows building isomorphism and verifying multiplication. Library syntax: GEN algsplit(GEN al, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplittingdata(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given central simple algebra al defined by multiplication table over its center K, returns stored data [t, Lbas, Lbasinv] used to compute a splitting of al over an extension: t ∈ al with L = K(t) a maximal subfield, Lbas matrix expressing an L-basis of al on integral basis, and Lbasinv expressing integral basis on L-basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show t and matrix sizes. Library syntax: GEN algsplittingdata(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplittingfield(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns an rnf structure: the splitting field of al stored in al, as a relative extension of the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows algsplittingfield(A).pol equals x^2 - y. Library syntax: GEN algsplittingfield(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsqr(al, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its square x^2 in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts square matrices with coefficients in al. Example and library syntax: GEN algsqr(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsub(al, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two elements x and y in al, computes their difference x - y in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example and library syntax: GEN algsub(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsubalg(al, B)
rubrics_metrics.description: al being a table algebra output by algtableinit and B a basis matrix of a subalgebra of al, computes an algebra al2 isomorphic to B and returns [al2, B2] where B2 is possibly different basis for al2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show reducing dimension and returned basis. Library syntax: GEN algsubalg(GEN al, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtableinit(mt, {p = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes the associative algebra over K = Q (p omitted) or Fp defined by multiplication table mt (t_VEC of n matrices in Mn(K) giving left multiplications by basis elements). Assumes e1 = 1 and integrality when K=Q. Main use: input finite dimensional K-algebra to compute radical and split quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides algebra object containing characteristic, multiplication table, traces. Examples include 2×2 upper triangular matrices. Library syntax: GEN algtableinit(GEN mt, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtensor(al1, al2, {maxord = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two algebras al1 and al2, computes their tensor product (over common center K). Currently only implemented for cyclic algebras of coprime degree over same center. Computes maximal order by default unless maxord=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN algtensor(GEN al1, GEN al2, long maxord).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtomatrix(al, x, {abs = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, returns the image of x under a homomorphism to a matrix algebra. If al is table algebra or abs=1 returns left multiplication matrix on integral basis; if al central simple and abs=0 returns φ(x) where φ : A ⊗K L → M_d(L) is an isomorphism stored in al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts square matrices with coefficients in al. Examples show different abs settings. Library syntax: GEN algtomatrix(GEN al, GEN x, long abs).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtrace(al, x, {abs = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its trace. If al is a table algebra or abs = 1, returns absolute trace (in Fp or Q); if al from alginit and abs = 0, returns the reduced trace in the center of al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show both reduced and absolute traces and relation with nfelttrace. Also accepts square matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algtrace(GEN al, GEN x, long abs).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtype(al)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al output by alginit or algtableinit, returns an integer indicating type: 0 not a valid algebra; 1 table algebra (algtableinit); 2 central simple algebra (alginit) represented by multiplication table over its center; 3 central simple algebra (alginit) represented by a cyclic algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show algtype([])=0 and types 1,2,3 for various constructions. Library syntax: long algtype(GEN al).
